coverage.note: Two items named no street address: a Chuseok festival at the Ferry Building, which is a venue mention of the kind news/AGENTS.md declines, and a report of gunfire at an unnamed apartment residence, which gives no address and is a crime story besides. The 3300 Geary story also names 2800 Geary Boulevard, 5420 Geary Boulevard and 3333 California Street, all three in a closing round-up of other projects along the corridor and all three sourced to SF YIMBY rather than reported here. They are not findings: the headline is the entry, and this headline is about the Jordan Park site. Each of those buildings needs its own story before it earns anything.

findings.description: An eight-storey, 84-foot condominium building is proposed for this corner site in Jordan Park, and the San Francisco Planning Department will have six months to approve it once the application is deemed complete. Updated filings show 89 for-sale condominiums, 13 of them deed-restricted affordable, with about 1,400 square feet of retail and 53 stacker parking spaces. The site is the former Hong Kong Lounge II, destroyed in February 2019 when an excavation crew ruptured a marked PG&E gas line at Geary Boulevard and Parker Avenue; the resulting three-alarm fire burned for more than two hours and damaged five structures, and the NTSB later cited the contractor's excavation practices. The lot has been vacant since. Two earlier proposals for the site called for 41 and then 62 units; the count reached 89 under the Family Zoning Plan, enacted January 2026, which also cut the project's affordable requirement from 15% to 5%. The design team and the ownership entity are recorded in extra rather than in the page's building block, because this is a proposal and no such building stands here — news/AGENTS.md is explicit that a proposal leaves its team out of building. The neighbours, merchants and residents quoted in the story are not recorded here.
